slot.brief: Series LCR circuit with given R, L, C and applied rms voltage at a stated frequency; compute the impedance (or power factor) by direct substitution.

stem: A series LCR circuit has $R=2\ \Omega$, $L=\dfrac{1}{50\pi}$ H and $C=\dfrac{1}{100\pi}$ F. It is connected to a $10$ V rms source of frequency $50$ Hz. What is the impedance?

verdicts.working: At 50 Hz, ω = 100π rad/s. Thus XL = 2 Ω and XC = 1 Ω, so Z = √(R² + (XL − XC)²) = √5 Ω.

working:
$X_L=2\pi fL=2\ \Omega$, $X_C=\dfrac{1}{2\pi fC}=1\ \Omega$. $Z=\sqrt{R^2+(X_L-X_C)^2}=\sqrt{2^2+1^2}=\sqrt{5}\ \Omega$.

Independent check: At 50 Hz, ω = 100π rad/s. Thus XL = 2 Ω and XC = 1 Ω, so Z = √(R² + (XL − XC)²) = √5 Ω.
solution:
For a series LCR circuit, $Z=\sqrt{R^2+(X_L-X_C)^2}$, where $X_L=2\pi fL=2\,\Omega$ and $X_C=\dfrac{1}{2\pi fC}=1\,\Omega$.
$$Z=\sqrt{2^2+(2-1)^2}=\sqrt{5}\,\Omega$$
